g.title: Before: the calendar decided, with silent gaps and full reloads gaps nobody saw.
Step 1: a traditional Glue job connects to the Salesforce API. It fetches data on a fixed calendar window, not on what is already in the target, so it cannot tell what it has already loaded.
Step 2: the job fetches past days of data from the API, a fixed window of past days, every run, whether those days changed or not.
Step 3: high risk of missing data when the job fails, or on API consistency issues, or for any other reason, and the missed changes are not noticed.
Step 4: the missed changes stay silent, so downstream data goes stale and nobody knows which days are missing.
Step 5: the only recovery is to perform a full load, which is slow and expensive, and SRC had been appended with slow and expensive, so the same record could load more than once.
No daily check on freshness, so stale data was found by users, not by the pipeline.

svg.text: How it happens, step by step — follow the numbered nodes in order; each step hands its problems to the next.

g.title: After: the data decides — watermark catch-up, idempotent upserts, and self-healing after outages.

Data fetching from API: steps 1-3 below are one sub-level group. Collapsed, this is just Salesforce API -> Glue custom downloader. Click to expand in the README / Explorer to see the 3 steps: Athena MAX(timestamp) watermark, build the API query per table from the watermark, call the API for only the changes since the watermark.

svg.text: Data fetching from API (click to expand in README / Explorer)
Collapsed view: Salesforce API -> Glue custom downloader

g.title: Step 1: for each table, run Athena MAX(timestamp) on the target to get the watermark, the latest timestamp already loaded. The data, not the calendar, decides where the next load starts.
Step 2: build the Salesforce API query per table from that watermark, with a small overlap, so a change right on the boundary is not missed.
Step 3: call the Salesforce API with that query, fetching only changes since the watermark, not a full load. This is what makes the delta cheap instead of a typical full pull.
Step 4: custom Glue downloaders call the API per object and land responses as JSON in the raw layer, exactly as the API returned them, so nothing is lost.
Step 5: schema check, then the SRC job writes Parquet, overwriting that day’s load, so a re-run is safe and clean and bad shapes are stopped early.

Step 6: the PRE job upserts, deduping on record Id and keeping the latest timestamp, loading each Id once as a create or an update, with full history kept. Idempotent upserts make overlaps and replays safe.
Step 7: the SEM job promotes PRE to SEM, Iceberg to Iceberg, fast, applying deletes via is_deleted, so SEM is current while PRE keeps history.
Step 8: DQ check daily at noon on the timestamp field, alerting if no new data arrived, so staleness is caught by the pipeline, not by users.

Step 9: self-healing — if down 1 day or 10, the next run resumes from the watermark, no gaps, no full reloads, because idempotent upserts make overlaps and replays safe. Consumers (dashboards and ML) read SEM.

svg.text: Why this beats a typical calendar delta: the data decides the start date, not the calendar, so a missed day does not silently lose changes. Consumers: dashboards and ML read SEM.
